newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE army signs $29 million in deals.
newsitem.headline: UAE army signs $29 million in deals.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates army said on Tuesday it signed deals worth $29 million with local and foreign firms, including one for coastal radars.
The deals, announced during the Gulf Arab state's IDEX 97 arms show, included a 14.8 million dirham ($4 million) training contract for nurses of the armed forces, the army said in a statement.

It signed a 47 million dirham contract to use natural gas to operate air conditioners with Gulf Energy System, a joint venture between a local company and France's Giat Industries set up under a tank deal offset obligation.
Giat clinched a $3.62 billion deal in 1993 to supply the UAE with battle tanks.
The army also signed a $12.3 million deal with Norway's Kongsberg Norcontrol Systems AS to buy coastal radars, the statement added without giving further details.
International arms manufacturers supplying the UAE are required to invest a portion of a deal's worth in profitable ventures with a UAE partner under the terms of the offset scheme.
The UAE Offsets Group (UOG) was launched in July 1990 when the UAE activated a plan to buy high-tech weapons worth billions of dollars.
